chunks: And with this chain, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ishaq al-Batihhi, who said:

I saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) pray the last 'Isha prayer before the disappearance of the twilight (shafaq), then he set out. These narrations carry two meanings: one is that they are specific to the state of necessity, which is for one who knows or suspects that if he does not pray at this time and waits for the disappearance of the twilight, he will not be able to do so due to an obstacle that stands between him and the prayer, or a preventer that prevents him from it, and that which indicates that.
ai.seo_question: When is the last 'Isha prayer time according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the permissibility of praying the last 'Isha before the complete disappearance of the evening twilight (shafaq), a practice central to the Shia view of prayer times. The text clarifies that this specific timing may be understood as a concession for necessity (darurah) or for those who fear being prevented from praying if they wait, highlighting the jurisprudential flexibility between strict timing and practical ease.
